entry.title: Location Matters: Sparse Latent-Variance Attacks for Face Privacy against Diffusion Personalization
entry.summary:
Text-to-image diffusion models can learn and reproduce an individual's identity from only a few reference photos, creating risks of unauthorized and misleading content generation. Proactive defenses address this risk by adding adversarial perturbations to facial images before release, thereby disrupting identity acquisition during downstream personalization. However, existing methods typically rely on dense $L_\infty$-bounded perturbations, whose accumulated distortions can become visible around facial structures.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #computer-vision #clean-tech

entry.title: Sable: A Small-Field Sumcheck Argument for Bit-Exact Inference of Large Language Models
entry.summary:
We present Sable, an argument system and single-GPU prover for the statement that a committed, integer-quantized transformer produced a given token sequence from a given prompt, bit for bit. Sable fixes an integer function F_O with no floating-point step, in which every rounding, normalization, softmax and sampling decision is determined by its inputs, and proves it with a constraint system whose relations provably never wrap modulo the 31-bit KoalaBear prime. The proof batches zerochecks and LogUp-GKR lookups into one sumcheck per domain, and commits to every witness tensor and weight in one multilinear commitment built from Reed-Solomon codes, BLAKE3 Merkle trees and a mixed-length BaseFold opening.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #ml-theory #number-theory

entry.title: Smaller Share Size for Evolving Secret Sharing: General Thresholds and Threshold Three
entry.summary:
Evolving secret sharing allows participants to join indefinitely without modifying previously distributed shares. We study the share size of perfectly secure evolving threshold secret sharing schemes and obtain two results. For general thresholds, we introduce a polynomial sharing method that shares two secrets with adjacent reconstruction thresholds using one polynomial.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #distributed-systems

entry.title: Revisiting Witness-Succinct UC-lifting Compilers
entry.summary:
Zero-knowledge succinct non-interactive arguments of knowledge (zkSNARKs) are increasingly used within larger cryptographic protocols, making security under composition essential. Generic compilation to Universal Composability (UC) requires straight-line, black-box extraction while preserving succinctness and controlling prover cost. We introduce verifiable reconstructible straightline codes (VRSCs), a primitive that separates public hiding, transcript-based reconstruction, binding, and proof non-rerandomizability.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #compilers #logic

entry.title: More Keys, Less Commitment: Key-Committing Attacks on BBB Accordions via Encode-then-Encipher and a Key-Committing Transform
entry.summary:
Cryptographic accordions with beyond-birthday-bound (BBB) security are being actively studied in connection with NIST’s ongoing standardization effort. We show that BBB security of an accordion does not necessarily strengthen key commitment of AE built from it: in many BBB accordions, additional keys introduced for BBB security give an adversary extra degrees of freedom. Exploiting this observation, we present $O(1)$ key-committing attacks on a broad range of AE schemes built from BBB accordions, mostly via the Encode-then-Encipher (EtE) paradigm, including CHCTR2, eCTR-based accordions, THCTR, HCTR+, TCT2, and bbb-ddd-AES under a natural polynomial-hash instantiation.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #combinatorics #infosec

entry.title: A Note on the Security of Changing of the Guards. Masking stands as one of the most effective countermeasures against side-channel attacks.
entry.summary:
Masking stands as one of the most effective countermeasures against side-channel attacks. The Changing of the Guards (COTG) technique reduces online fresh randomness by reusing masks and borrowing shares across nonlinear computations. We identify a security flaw in the round-based AES Design I of Askeland et al.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: PERSEPHONE: Zero-Knowledge Multiplicative Non-Negative Proof for Sequential Private Range Verification
entry.summary:
Privacy is a fundamental requirement of modern digital payment systems, which process highly sensitive financial data, including account balances and transaction amounts. Unauthorized disclosure of this information can compromise users’ financial privacy and expose them to fraud or other forms of financial abuse. A key challenge in this setting is to verify that a payment amount does not exceed the payer’s available balance without revealing either the payment amount or the balance.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #infosec
